_note: Current provisional FATES-005D-R1 candidate. This is a post-durable-identity/dispatch/reconciliation remediation bounded vertical, not a seal or a claim of general exactly-once execution.

adrasteia.role: portable runtime contracts, canonical context, receipt and binding representation

ananke.role: authenticated authority, policy, content preflight and signed authority receipt

mnemosyne.role: durable authenticated receipt replay and strict source-bound memory admission

horae.role: durable governed lifecycle, direct principal binding, single-dispatch ownership and controlled-effect reconciliation

moirae-code.role: controlled host/guest-shaped request envelope; no direct provider execution in this vertical

integration.role: non-recursive control identity; final R1 publication commit is recorded separately from this manifest

candidateOperation.name: governed.memory-admission
candidateOperation.effectModel: durable intent plus stable-ID authoritative reconcilable local controlled sink
candidateOperation.freshness: local fixed-clock receipt validity; expired evidence fails closed

securityBinding.operationBinding: canonical SHA-256 over operation ID, correlation, authenticated principal id/kind and acting principal id/kind, tenant, workspace, project, action, source/memory resource, destination and input digest
securityBinding.freshnessPolicy: Ananke/Mnemosyne receipt validation uses issuedAt/expiresAt under the bounded local clock; expired or malformed authority is rejected
securityBinding.replayPolicy: IDEMPOTENT_SAME_EFFECT for an identical durable operation binding; changed payload, caller, acting principal or scope is rejected and receipt reuse is rejected after restart
securityBinding.artifactVerification: Runtime Contracts artifact is SHA-256 verified when materialized; source and artifact identities are recorded separately

notes: FATES-005D-R1 provisional candidate r6: the selected governed.memory-admission operation directly binds authenticated and acting principals into Horae durable identity, arbitrates effect dispatch with a durable cross-process claim, and treats stale claims and post-boundary uncertainty as reconciliation-required. The controlled local sink has a stable ledger identity, checksum-protected schema, atomic mutation locking and authoritative CONFIRMED/ABSENT/UNKNOWN semantics; missing, replaced or corrupt evidence cannot authorize redispatch. The candidate remains local and bounded: it is not a distributed exactly-once guarantee, a power-loss proof, a Firecracker/KVM acceptance, a containment proof, a Qwen/model validation, a production readiness claim or a seal. The Integration control commit is intentionally non-recursive and points to the already-published r5 implementation/control checkpoint; the final R1 publication commit containing this manifest is reported separately.
knownLimits: The durable stores use atomic local filesystem state and locks; distributed database, multi-host and arbitrary power-loss guarantees are not claimed.
The controlled effect is a deterministic local sink with stable identity and reconciliation; arbitrary external providers are not covered.
The bounded vertical proves one governed operation and the named local crash/concurrency boundaries, not every Fates operation or every restart boundary in production.
The Moirae path is host/guest-shaped but no Firecracker guest launch, jailer boundary, vsock-only proof or VM escape proof was performed.
Host credential custody, network isolation and direct-provider impossibility require the future Linux/KVM acceptance environment.
Ananke metadata still advertises a stale 0.4.0 Runtime Contracts range in one adapter while its actual dependency is 0.6.2; this candidate records the mismatch without changing Ananke.
No Qwen/model integration, external provider call, release tag, seal or production-readiness claim is made.
